elements.id-string-16: This paper presents \system\footnote{\primitiveprefix, pronounced ``bab-ka'', loosely stands for Byzantine Broadcast with Commit-Adopt.},a Byzantine log replication technology for partially synchronous networks enabling blocks to be broadcast in parallel,such that each broadcast is \emph{finalized} independently and instantaneously into an individual slot in the log.Every finalized broadcast is eventually \emph{committed} to the total ordering,so that all network bandwidth has utility in disseminating blocks.Finalizing log slots in parallel achieves both high throughput and low latency.\system is composed of two principal protocols that interweave together, a low-latency/high-throughput happy path, and a high-throughput DAG-based fallback path.The happy path employs a novel primitive called \primitive,a consistent broadcast enforcing unique slot numbering.In steady state, \primitive ensures that a transaction can be committed with low latency, in just 3 network steps.Under network partitions or faults,we harness recent advances in BFT and builda fallback mechanism on a direct acyclic graph (DAG) created by \primitive broadcasts.In this manner, \system exhibits the throughput benefits of DAG-based BFT in face of gaps.

elements.id-string-22: They allow parallel broadcasts to proceed for a while, and then wait for a leader to drive a commit decision on an entire ``wave'' of accumulated broadcasts.

elements.id-string-206: \textit{Integrity}: If a correct validator \primitivesmall-delivers $(id, sn, b)$ and the sender $p$ is correct, then $p$ had previously invoked \primitivesmall-bcast for $(id, sn, b)$.\textit{No-duplication}: Every correct validator \primitivesmall-delivers at most once per instance.\textit{Consistency}: If a correct validator $p$ \primitivesmall-delivers $(\bm{id}, sn, b)$ and a correct $q$ validator \primitivesmall-delivers $(\bm{id}, sn', b')$  for the same instance $id$, then $b=b'$ and $sn=sn'$ .\textit{Unique sequencing}: If a correct validator $p$ \primitivesmall-delivers $(id, \bm{sn}, b)$ and a correct validator $q$  \primitivesmall-delivers $(id', \bm{sn}, b')$ for the same non-nil slot number $sn \in \mathbb{N}$, then $id=id'$ (and by Consistency also $b=b'$).\textit{Validity}: If a correct validator $p$ \primitivesmall-bcasts $(id, sn, b)$ then eventually every correct validator \primitivesmall-delivers $(id, sn', b)$, such that either $sn'=sn \in\mathbb{N}$ or $sn'=\emptyslot$.\textit{Weak Sequencing Validity}: After GST, if a correct validator $p$ \primitivesmall-bcasts $(id, sn, b)$ with $sn\in\mathbb{N}$, no other validator \primitivesmall-bcasts $(id',sn, b')$,and no correct validator incurs $\bbcaabort(sn)$,then every correct validator delivers $(id, sn, b)$.\textit{External Validity:} If some correct validator \primitivesmall-delivers $(id, sn, b)$ then $\mathcal{P}(b)$ is \true.\textit{Finalization:} If some correct validator $p$ incurs $\bbcaabort(sn)$ with $sn \in\mathbb{N}$, then $p$ incurs $\bbcaannounce$.Moreover, if $2f+1$ validators with indexes in set $I$ incur$\bbcaannounce(id_i, sn, b_i, \pi_i, \mathcal{Q})$ such that $\mathcal{Q}(\bigcup_{i\in I}\{\pi_i\})=\false$, then no correct node \primitivesmall-delivers $(id, sn, b)$ for any $id$ and block $b$.

elements.id-string-352: Key to the good performance of system is an effective way for allocating sequence slots to validators exclusively.
elements.id-string-353: Otherwise, sender broadcasts might ``collide'' in their attempted sequence slots.
elements.id-string-354: It is important to note that in case of collisions, broadcasts are not lost:
elements.id-string-355: However, this scenario will suffer the same commit delay as previous protocols, which rely on a leader to commit a wave of accumulated broadcasts; we want to avoid this in \system.
elements.id-string-356: Additionally, eventually blocks carrying sequence numbers need to be enabled for the system to make progress.
elements.id-string-357: To this end, we introduce an abstract functionality referred to as a \emph{ticketmaster}.
elements.id-string-358: The goal of a ticketmaster is to assign sequence slots to actively brodcasting validators, hereon referred to as active validators, exclusively and consecutively.
elements.id-string-359: In order to prevent Byzantine validators from capriciously attempting to \primitivesmall-bcast sequence numbers,
elements.id-string-361: validators should be allowed to invoke \bbcacast\ only with their sequence slots.
